full_judgment:
This Rule was issued on an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act. 

 3. Mr Abul Kalam Mainuddin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that he has explained the reasons for delay in paragraph No.6 of the application and the said delay should be condoned in view of the provision of Article 181 of the Limitation Act providing a period of 3 years for making such revisional application as there is no specific period prescribed for filing a revisional application. In support of his submission, the learned Advocate has (sic) referred the decisions in the case between Md Swaleh and another vs United Crain & Fodder Agencies, reported in 16 DLR (SC) 155 and in the case between Nadira Rahman Vs Sayed Amir Hossain, reported in 35 DLR 277. 

 7. The appellate Court below passed the impugned judgment and decree on 6-9-2001 dismissing the appeal. The statement made in paragraph No.6 of the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act explaining the delay as aforesaid is a vague and indefinite statement and far from satisfactory explanation. The submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that there is no prescribed period of limitation for filing a revisional application can only be considered on a satisfactory and cogent explanation of delay caused in filing such an application. The decision in the case between Muhammad Swaleh and another Vs United Grain & Fodder Agencies, reported in 16 DLR (SC) 155 followed in the case of Nadira Rahman vs Sayed Amir Hossain, reported in 35 DLR 277 has no manner of application in the facts of the instant case wherein it has been held as under: 

 "The Limitation Act does not provide for any period of limitation for an application in revision. The only article which could be applicable was the residuary Article 181 which provides a limitation of three years for an application but even that Article will not stand in the way of the exercise of revisional power for these powers can be exercised suo motu." 

 "The above observation is not to be understood to have laid down any law that Article 181 of the Limitation Act, 1908 governs an application under section 115 of the Civil Procedure Code. It merely laid down emphasis on the principle that the High Court's power to revise an order suo motu is not restricted by any time limit." 

 11. The aforesaid rulings of our apex Court have specifically laid down the cardinal principle of the discretional exercise of the power of the High Court Division in condoning the delay in a suitable case where/there is no negligence and laches on the part of the petitioner in filing a revisional application before it beyond the statutory period of 90 days prescribed for filing a civil appeal only on satisfactory explanation of delay. In the instant case, as already stated above, the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act does not bear a cogent and satisfactory explanation. The explanation offered by the petitioner appears totally vague, obscure and indefinite which is a testimony of clear negligence and laches on his part in pursuing the proceeding instead of with due diligence and bona fide. The statement explaining the delay made in paragraph 6 of the application as stated above does not give me any opportunity to deviate from the aforesaid long standing settled practice of our Court in condoning the instant inordinate delay of 960 days in making the revisional application in this Court. In that view of the matter I find no merit in the Rule and the same is liable to be discharged.
